---
name: Lesson feedback
about: Something in the tutorial confused you
title: 'lesson: '
labels: learning
assignees: ''
---

**Where**

Which lesson, and the sentence or diagram you stopped at. Quoting the line is
better than describing it.

**What confused you**

In whatever words you would use out loud. "I do not know what this symbol is",
"I could not tell if the arrow means before or after", and "I read it four times
and it did not go in" are all complete and useful answers.

**What you thought it meant**

Only if you have a guess. A wrong reading that seemed reasonable is the single
most valuable thing in this box — it shows where the prose admits an
interpretation it did not intend.

**Where you were**

Roughly how far into the material, and whether you had met any of this before.

---

**A confused reader is data, not a complaint.** This tutorial is written from
[`docs/learner-failure-log.md`](../../docs/learner-failure-log.md) — a record of
where one real learner actually got stuck — rather than from a table of contents.
Your confusion is the next entry.

Lesson prose is by invitation for now, so this is the most direct way to change
what the lessons say. If the text lost you, the text is wrong.
